variants.title: Follow one objective from evidence to use
variants.context: Both families move through the same four stages: observe an input under a versioned schema, choose the learning target, estimate parameters, then use the learned object by returning a prediction directly or by conditioning and marginalizing a distribution.
variants.prompt: A payments team builds a direct risk score. Put the four stages in order.

items.text: Return the score at request time and let the payment policy turn it into approve, decline, or review.
Choose the direct conditional objective, which estimates the probability of fraud given those features.
Fit the weights and bias so that observed labels receive high conditional probability.
Collect authorization features under a versioned schema: amount, merchant, device identity, and velocity counters.

variants.hint: The learning target is settled before any parameter is fitted.
variants.explanation: Evidence, objective, estimation, use. The discriminative path never has to explain how the features themselves are distributed.

variants.title: Follow one objective from evidence to use
variants.context: Both families move through the same four stages: observe an input under a versioned schema, choose the learning target, estimate parameters, then use the learned object by returning a prediction directly or by conditioning and marginalizing a distribution.
variants.prompt: A reliability team builds a Gaussian Naive Bayes fault detector. Put the four stages in order.

items.text: Choose the class conditional objective, which learns how readings behave inside each class alongside the class prior.
Collect machine readings under a versioned schema: temperature, vibration, and current draw.
Combine likelihood with prior through Bayes' rule to return a posterior over healthy and fault.
Estimate one mean and one variance per feature and class, plus each class prior.

variants.hint: A generative model reaches a class only after it has learned how features behave.
variants.explanation: The generative path spends its capacity describing the data process first, then conditions that description to produce a decision.

variants.title: Follow one objective from evidence to use
variants.context: Both families move through the same four stages: observe an input under a versioned schema, choose the learning target, estimate parameters, then use the learned object by returning a prediction directly or by conditioning and marginalizing a distribution.
variants.prompt: A simulator team needs plausible completions of partial sensor traces. Put the four stages in order.

items.text: Condition on the observed part of a new trace and sample the missing segment for the simulator.
Choose an objective that models the distribution of whole traces rather than one target label.
Estimate the latent structure that explains the observed traces.
Collect complete historical traces under a versioned schema, with provenance and effective time attached.

variants.hint: The product asks for new observations, not for a label.
variants.explanation: Sampling and completion need a distribution over observations, which is exactly the structure the generative objective pays to learn.

variants.title: Move a bundle down the production path
variants.context: The lesson orders the production path as product contract, data contract, learning objective, inference boundary, and outcome monitor. Every boundary carries a version, an owner, a validation contract, and a rollback path.
variants.prompt: A new fault classifier is going to production for the first time. Put the boundaries in order.

items.text: Enforce the inference boundary: validate inputs, apply timeouts and resource budgets, and attach model lineage to every output.
Write the product contract: the exact output, the accepted abstention behavior, the latency budget, and the downstream owner.
Pin the learning objective: loss, family, assumptions, preprocessing, calibration, and seeds, stored with the trained parameters.
Watch the outcome monitor: task quality, calibration, drift, slices, latency, cost, and downstream harm before the bundle is promoted.
Version the data contract: feature meaning, missingness, label delay, consent, retention, and the train and serve transformations.

variants.hint: Which boundary decides what all the later ones are allowed to produce?
variants.explanation: The product contract comes first because the required output, abstention rule, and latency budget constrain the data, objective, and serving choices below it.

variants.title: Move a bundle down the production path
variants.context: The lesson orders the production path as product contract, data contract, learning objective, inference boundary, and outcome monitor. Every boundary carries a version, an owner, a validation contract, and a rollback path.
variants.prompt: A support tool will use a generative model to draft replies. Put the boundaries in order.

items.text: Version the evidence: which conversations may be used, consent, retention, and one normalization shared by both paths.
Bound the inference call: cap sample count, output size, retries, and execution time, and record lineage on each draft.
Measure what shipped: human acceptance, harmful output rate, leakage checks, latency, and cost before wider release.
Release the objective as one artifact: model, preprocessing, sampling settings, and seeds pinned together.
Define what the product accepts: a draft that a human approves, never an automatic send.

variants.hint: A generated proposal only earns authority the product contract already granted it.
variants.explanation: The same five boundaries apply to generation, and the first one is where the rule that a draft is not a side effect is written down.

variants.title: Move a bundle down the production path
variants.context: The lesson orders the production path as product contract, data contract, learning objective, inference boundary, and outcome monitor. Every boundary carries a version, an owner, a validation contract, and a rollback path.
variants.prompt: Operations wants to ship a recalibrated version of a deployed classifier. Put the boundaries in order.

items.text: Compare the outcome monitors of both bundles, then promote the new one or restore the previous one.
Re-pin the objective bundle with the new calibration and class priors recorded beside the weights.
Confirm the data contract: online feature definitions and missing value rules still match what training used.
Replay the inference boundary on representative and adversarial slices while the previous bundle stays deployable.
Confirm the product contract is unchanged: same output, same abstention rule, same deadline.

variants.hint: Even a small change walks the same boundaries in the same order.
variants.explanation: Calibration and priors are versioned separately from raw weights, but they still travel the whole path before they get authority.

variants.title: Count what the objective must estimate
variants.context: For K classes and d numeric features, multiclass logistic regression estimates K times d feature weights plus one bias per class, while Gaussian Naive Bayes estimates one mean and one variance per feature and class plus one prior per class.
variants.prompt: A Gaussian Naive Bayes model is trained for 4 classes over 12 numeric features. How many values does it estimate in total?
variants.hint: Count what one class needs, then multiply by the number of classes.
variants.explanation: Each class needs 12 means, 12 variances, and 1 prior, which is 25 values, and 4 classes give 100.

mistakes.feedback: That leaves out the one prior per class.
That counts a mean per feature and a prior but forgets the variances.

variants.title: Count what the objective must estimate
variants.context: For K classes and d numeric features, multiclass logistic regression estimates K times d feature weights plus one bias per class, while Gaussian Naive Bayes estimates one mean and one variance per feature and class plus one prior per class.
variants.prompt: A multiclass logistic regression is trained for 5 classes over 30 numeric features. How many direct coefficients does it estimate?
variants.hint: Each class carries a weight per feature and something extra.
variants.explanation: Each class needs 30 feature weights plus 1 bias, which is 31, and 5 classes give 155.

mistakes.feedback: That forgets the one bias per class.
That counts a single class instead of all five.

variants.title: Count what the objective must estimate
variants.context: For K classes and d numeric features, multiclass logistic regression estimates K times d feature weights plus one bias per class, while Gaussian Naive Bayes estimates one mean and one variance per feature and class plus one prior per class.
variants.prompt: A three class problem has 20 numeric features. How many more values does Gaussian Naive Bayes estimate than multiclass logistic regression on the same problem?
variants.hint: Work out both totals first, then compare them.
variants.explanation: Gaussian Naive Bayes estimates 3 times 41, which is 123, and logistic regression estimates 3 times 21, which is 63, so the extra structure costs 60 values.

mistakes.feedback: That drops the three class priors before subtracting.
That adds the two totals instead of comparing them.

variants.title: Pick the objective from the output contract
variants.context: Choose the narrowest learning objective that can produce the required output under the real data and serving constraints. A richer distribution is worth paying for only when the product actually uses that extra structure.
variants.prompt: A payments team needs a calibrated risk score for every authorization, and years of labeled chargebacks already exist. Which objective fits the output contract?
options: A generative objective chosen so the team can also sample synthetic authorizations later.
A discriminative objective that estimates the probability of fraud given the observed features.
A generative objective that models how authorizations are distributed inside each class.
optionFeedback: Wrong. Sampling is not in the output contract, so paying for that structure buys operational risk instead of product value.
Correct. The product consumes a calibrated conditional score and representative labels exist, so the narrowest objective already produces it.
Wrong. Modeling the feature distribution adds assumptions the score does not use and that must then be tested.
variants.hint: Start from what the downstream software actually consumes.
variants.explanation: Choose the narrowest objective that produces the required output, because extra distributional structure has to be validated even when nothing consumes it.

variants.title: Pick the objective from the output contract
variants.context: Choose the narrowest learning objective that can produce the required output under the real data and serving constraints. A richer distribution is worth paying for only when the product actually uses that extra structure.
variants.prompt: A reliability team must fill in missing segments of sensor traces and sample plausible traces to stress a simulator. Which objective fits?
options: A discriminative regressor trained to predict only the next single reading of the trace.
A generative objective that models the distribution of traces so it can complete and sample them.
A discriminative classifier over trace types, with the winning type's average trace copied in.
optionFeedback: Wrong. Predicting one reading ahead does not give a distribution over whole missing segments.
Correct. Completion and sampling need a distribution over observations, which is what the generative objective learns.
Wrong. A class label plus an average trace produces neither a plausible completion nor the diversity a simulator needs.
variants.hint: Ask whether the product needs an answer or new observations.
variants.explanation: Sampling, reconstruction, and completion are exactly the operations that justify learning a data distribution.

variants.title: Pick the objective from the output contract
variants.context: Choose the narrowest learning objective that can produce the required output under the real data and serving constraints. A richer distribution is worth paying for only when the product actually uses that extra structure.
variants.prompt: A support tool drafts a reply and must also decide whether that reply may be sent without a human. What is the sound design?
options: Let the single generative model emit the draft and its own decision about sending it.
Let the generator write the draft and treat any well formed output as approved to send.
Keep two models: a generator for the draft and a direct classifier for the send decision.
optionFeedback: Wrong. A model that grades its own output makes the generation objective the authorization boundary too.
Wrong. Format validity is not policy approval, and a generated proposal must not become a side effect on its own.
Correct. One component predicts a decision and another generates an artifact, so they stay separate models with separate contracts.
variants.hint: One model does not need to own every product behavior.
variants.explanation: Separating the generator from the decision keeps the authority to act with a component that was trained and evaluated for that decision.

variants.title: Handle missing evidence
variants.context: Missing evidence is part of the model contract. A system can reject and route elsewhere, impute a versioned value that ships with the model, or marginalize an unobserved variable under a learned probability model with confidence that reflects the thinner evidence.
variants.prompt: A Gaussian Naive Bayes fault model receives a request in which every sensor reading is absent. The posterior would return the class prior, 82 percent healthy and 18 percent fault. What should the service do?
options: Serve the prior as the prediction, because it is the mathematically consistent posterior here.
Impute the training mean for every sensor and serve the posterior that results from those fills.
Abstain and route to review, because a prior only answer carries no evidence about this machine.
optionFeedback: Wrong. Consistency is not usefulness, and serving it disguises an empty answer as a current prediction.
Wrong. Imputing every feature manufactures evidence the request never supplied and hides that fact downstream.
Correct. The lesson calls the empty evidence case consistent but not automatically useful, so an explicit abstain state belongs in the contract.
variants.hint: Ask how much evidence about this specific case reached the model.
variants.explanation: A prior only posterior contains no observation, so the degraded state is to abstain, request evidence, or hand the case to review.

variants.title: Handle missing evidence
variants.context: Missing evidence is part of the model contract. A system can reject and route elsewhere, impute a versioned value that ships with the model, or marginalize an unobserved variable under a learned probability model with confidence that reflects the thinner evidence.
variants.prompt: One of five readings is missing for a validated Gaussian Naive Bayes model, and the remaining four sit inside the trained support. What is the appropriate handling?
options: Fill the missing reading with the class mean of whichever class is currently most likely.
Omit that feature's likelihood term and let the posterior rest on the observed terms and the prior.
Reject the request, because a probability model needs every feature it was trained on.
optionFeedback: Wrong. Filling with a class conditional mean assumes the answer and pushes the posterior toward it.
Correct. Marginalizing an unobserved variable is what a probability model supports, with confidence reflecting the thinner evidence.
Wrong. Rejecting throws away four usable observations that the probability model can still score.
variants.hint: One family can integrate a variable away rather than inventing it.
variants.explanation: Marginalization works only as well as the learned distributions and independence assumptions, so it is validated like any other contract.

variants.title: Handle missing evidence
variants.context: Missing evidence is part of the model contract. A system can reject and route elsewhere, impute a versioned value that ships with the model, or marginalize an unobserved variable under a learned probability model with confidence that reflects the thinner evidence.
variants.prompt: A fixed input logistic classifier is already deployed and one feature is occasionally absent at request time. What belongs in the design?
options: A marginalization step over the missing feature carried out inside the deployed classifier.
A versioned fill policy with a missingness indicator, validated as part of the deployed bundle.
A request time default chosen by whichever calling service happens to find the field empty.
optionFeedback: Wrong. A direct conditional model has no distribution over the feature, so there is nothing to integrate out.
Correct. The fill policy can move the decision boundary, so it ships and is validated with the model.
Wrong. Callers picking their own defaults makes model behavior depend on code nobody evaluated.
variants.hint: Ask who owns the value the model sees when the field is empty.
variants.explanation: Imputation is part of the model contract, which is why the fill value and its indicator are versioned and replayed with the bundle.
